caption: Hebrews makes Jesus the representative human who begins to fulfil Psalm 8’s calling. It is powerful theology, but the psalm itself mentions no Messiah or death.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 8 predict Jesus’s rise? Psalm 8 places humanity below heavenly beings but crowns it with glory and rule. Hebrews applies that calling to Jesus.
slides.body: Psalm 8 places humanity below heavenly beings but crowns it with glory and rule. Hebrews applies that calling to Jesus.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 8 predict Jesus’s rise?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 8:5-6: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
slides.body: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor.
slides.heading: Ps 8:5-6

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Heb 2:5–9, BSB: We see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death.
slides.body: We see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Heb 2:5–9

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Hebrews makes a powerful case It quotes the passage, then says: “We see Jesus”—lowered, killed and now crowned with glory.
slides.body: It quotes the passage, then says: “We see Jesus”—lowered, killed and now crowned with glory.
slides.heading: Hebrews makes a powerful case

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the psalm speaks about humanity It mentions no future Messiah or death. Hebrews focuses humanity’s calling into the story of Jesus.
slides.body: It mentions no future Messiah or death. Hebrews focuses humanity’s calling into the story of Jesus.
slides.heading: But the psalm speaks about humanity

title: Lower, then crowned
